references.text: Jacob tells Pharaoh that he is 130 years old, which together with 17 years in Egypt gives his total lifespan of 147 years.
Abraham's total lifespan of 175 years, as a parallel to the summary of the patriarchs' lifespans.
Isaac's total lifespan of 180 years and his death, as a parallel to the summary of Jacob's lifespan.
Joseph's lifespan and death in Egypt, further paralleling the patriarchs' time in Egypt.
Stephen recounts that Jacob went down to Egypt and died there, a direct reference to Jacob's final years in Egypt.
Parallel conclusion of the patriarchs' life accounts: Jacob's 147 years and Joseph's 110 years mark the end of the generation that moved to Egypt.
The contrast between Jacob's individual stay (17 years) and the total duration of the people's stay (430 years) places the patriarch's life within the broader plan of salvation history.
Symmetrical conclusion of the patriarchs' life accounts: Jacob's 147 years and Joseph's 110 years emphasize that both died in Egypt as foreigners.
Direct narrative connection: Pharaoh asks about the number of years (v.8), and v.28 delivers the final summary of Jacob's lifespan.
